content.thinking:
I need to write this file carefully in one pass without testing. I'm planning the design: a hunched swamp troll about 2.6m tall in a chunky Warcraft style, with huge hands and shoulders, a small head, tusks, a mohawk, and bone fetishes like a necklace, belt skull, and totem, plus a loincloth and wrist wraps. Now I'm working out the skeleton structure starting from the hip root.

Setting up the joint chain...

For the jaw I'll place it just below the head with an aim target slightly forward. Rather than lofting a continuous mesh along the spine, I'll build the torso from simple rigid spheres bound to each bone — chest, belly, and pelvis spheres with tapering radii, plus shoulder spheres at the chest joint — since this is simpler and more robust than a full sweep.

For skin I'm layering a mottled green base with a lighter countershaded belly tone and darker mossy patches for texture. For the arms I'm defining a joint chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist using a curve through those points, which I'll then cap with a hand sphere.

Writing arm sweep and finger chains...

Still defining hand and leg geometry... now sizing the palm sphere and finger offsets, then setting up the two-segment leg chain with hip, knee, and ankle joints bending forward.

Next I'm placing the foot geometry with a scaled sphere for the sole and spiked toes with claws, checking that the leg's reach stays within its total length so the foot sits flush on the floor. Then I move to the head, positioning the skull sphere and starting on the brow ridge shape.

Now I'm building the muzzle and jaw structure, sketching the upper jaw sphere and a lower jaw piece with a chin, then sweeping curved tusk shapes with a bezier path tapering upward in ivory color, plus smaller secondary tusks and a small dark nose sphere.

Moving on to eyes with glowing yellow spheres and black pupils, pointed horizontal ear spikes extending outward with bone-colored material, ring earrings, small teeth cones along the lower jaw, and now sketching a mohawk of coarse spike-like hair running along the head and down the neck in deep red and dark tones following a curved path.

I'll scatter warts as small spheres across the belly, chest, and back surfaces, then move on to bone fetishes — building a necklace-like strand of bones along a curve following the chest's front contour.

Writing necklace geometry...

Now I'm thinking about the belt placement, sweeping a leather strap around the belly surface at a height that cuts across the belly sphere rather than the pelvis, so the loop sits naturally lower on the torso.

For the buckle, I'm positioning a small skull ornament on the belt's front where it projects outward from the belly curve, calculating the surface depth there geometrically. Then I'm sketching a hanging loincloth as an extruded outline from the belt's front point, but realizing it ends up floating since it's placed well in front of where the legs actually are — I need to rethink that placement so it drapes down to meet the body properly.

I'm adding a matching back flap at roughly the belt height but shifted to the rear-facing side of the pelvis, plus painted stripe texturing in earthy ochre and rust tones with bone-bead trim along the edges.

For the totem staff held in the figure's off-hand, I'm planning a vertical pole gripped at fist height, running from the ground up past head height, topped with a skull and decorated with dangling feathers, bones, and rope bindings.

I'm detailing the staff further, positioning it inside the curled fingers, adding bone cords, torus rings for the leather bindings at intervals, and a crossbar near the top with hanging teeth and bones. Now I'm planning a separate bone-tusk pauldron fetish for the shoulder, built from a spike cluster anchored with a leather strap.

Then I'm sketching out additional small accessories — leather wrist and ankle bands with bone beads, an upper-arm bone bangle — and considering adding a mossy hump and scattered lichen or mushroom blobs across the back for a swampy troll aesthetic, using clustered spheres for moss and simple cone-and-disc shapes for mushrooms.

Now I'm adding finishing details: bone-colored claws, a brow ridge capsule, and glowing yellow eyes, plus a decal-based war paint design with mirrored diagonal red stripes on each cheek and a rune marking on the chest.

Adding chest tattoo decal and jaw teeth...

I need to be careful to only import what I actually use—THREE, createBuilder, rng, and whatever shaping helpers end up needed—rather than padding imports. I'm also sketching a small blob helper that builds sphere-based parts with bone, position, radius, and color options.

Setting up imports and paint logic...

Building the spine chain...

Still placing torso bones...

Now I'm setting up the arm chains with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints positioned mirrored left/right off the chest, using tapering sweep radii for a natural limb shape.

Thinking about the hand next: the palm attaches to the wrist tip, and three fingers curl downward and forward from the palm front, each built as a two-segment chain with tapering radii and named per finger index and side.

I'm adding small claw spikes at each fingertip in a contrasting color, and shaping the thumb separately with its own shorter curling path on the opposite side of the palm.

Now I'm figuring out the staff placement in the right hand—positioning its pole so it threads naturally between the curled fingers without clipping through them, adjusting the radius and z-offset accordingly.

For the legs, I'm setting up hip-to-ankle chains with slightly bent knees, giving each leg joint names scoped by side and defining tapering sweep radii along the limb.

Now I'm adding foot blobs, spiky toes with slight splay per index, and claws jutting from each toe tip, before moving on to the floor geometry.

For the ankle, I'm thinking about adding a torus cuff near the ankle, positioned along the leg's knee-to-ankle segment using a lerp between those two points.

Now I'm shifting to the head geometry, placing the skull box and defining brow shapes as angled capsules on either side of the face, sloping down toward where the eye sockets will go.

Still placing facial features...

Adding tusk tip color bands, then placing small upper fangs near the head, and defining lower teeth and ear spikes with a torus accent at the ear base.

Adding gold hoop ring, then building the mohawk spikes along a path with alternating colors and tapering length based on position.

Refining the ridge sweep path points down the neck, chest, and back hump to sit correctly against each surface's radius.

For the mohawk, I'm setting 18 spikes with a red-to-orange gradient along a thin flat ridge base, then adding a decal with a spiral rune design to the chest surface using a green-tinted stroke.

Now I'm layering war paint slashes in dark red across the head decal, then moving to fetishes -- necklace, pendants, skull belt piece, staff totem, shoulder bone spikes, bangles, and hip tooth strings. For the necklace, I'm building a cord-colored rope path around the chest with bone capsule pendants spaced along it.

Computing neck anchor positions...

Placing the skull pendant beneath the belly, positioning eye sockets, nose, and jaw as small dark blobs, then adding a belt loop attached to the belly surface geometry.

Working out the belt sweep, buckle placement, and radius adjustments so the skull buckle sits correctly against the belly curve, then scattering rivets along the belt loop using frame-based point placement.

For the hanging bone decorations, I'm figuring out the loop parameterization—working out that counter-clockwise rotation about the +Y axis takes +Z toward +X, meaning t=0 is front-facing, t=.25 is the left side, t=.5 is back, and t=.75 is the right side, so I can place the dangling bones/teeth at the correct hip positions around the belt.

Still defining loincloth geometry...

Adjusting the flap height and thickness, then moving on to shoulder spikes—placing three bone spikes per shoulder with varied outward directions, and adding small moss and mushroom blobs scattered across the back for a weathered look.

I'll skip hanging moss and reeds, then scatter warts across the belly, chest, hump, and pelvis surfaces by embedding small spheres while avoiding collisions with other meshes. For accessories, I'm planning a gold torus bangle around the upper arm and a leather cuff torus at the wrist.

Now I'm working out the torus orientations for the forearm and upper arm cuffs, using the arm direction vector to align each ring's axis, and applying the same approach to ankle and leg cuffs with bone spikes.

I'm adding the staff pole, attaching it rigidly to the hand bone, and building the skull topper with jaw, eye sockets, horns, and bezier-swept feather shapes in teal and red.

I'm continuing to add detail: a lower bone crossbar, hanging bone-and-teeth strings, and torus cord bindings at various heights along the pole, then double-checking overall model height stays within bounds with the mohawk and staff included.

Now I'm adding small glow accents to the staff skull's eye sockets using a tiny green tint, confirming the color palette stays within limits, and defining the face details like eye and pupil colors. I'm also adding two side dreadlock braids sweeping from the head with bezier curves, tapering radius, dark red hair color, and bone ornaments at the tips.

For the skin, I'm layering a mottled green base with a countershaded lighter belly, then applying a gradient overlay to darken the lower legs and feet into muddy stains, while keeping arms and hands the same base skin tone. I'm being careful to only declare variables I actually use to avoid TypeScript errors as I build out the blob helper function with proper fill/color typing.

Now I'm sorting out imports, using type-only imports for the Paint type and deciding against sharing sphere geometry across parts to keep cloning behavior safe. I'm setting up the spike function call for limbs with base, tip, length, radius and color options, and starting to configure the war paint decal placement on the skull with position, direction, and size parameters.

Checking that decal positions land close to surface geometry for the skull cheek and chest, and sketching a torus-based ring helper for rings/collars using position, radius, tube, direction, and color. I'm planning to write out all the parts with loops over the side variable, and setting up a record type to track hand joints for the arms.

For the limb paths, I'll build point arrays and pass them into a chain function that generates smoothed polyline geometry with filleted corners at joints like knees. For fingers, I'll grab the arm's tip joint as the base position for the hand.
